land.text: the Brittonic coast between the Forth and the Tees before Ida

predecessors.note: The Bernicia page does not say who held the land before Ida; 'Bryneich' is the British name (Hen Ogledd page).

land.text: Bernicia united with Deira under Oswald

successors.note: 'Under Oswald son of Æthelfrith, Bernicia was united with Deira to form Northumbria from 634 onward.' Cliopatria's Northumbria already has a shape from 612 to 632 and again from 634.

capitals.name: Bamburgh
capitals.note: Infobox capital; the kingdom 'may have been ruled from the site that later became the English Bamburgh'. Nennius's name for the royal city is Din Guaire (Northumbria page).

rulers.name: Ida
rulers.note: Page: Ida 'obtained the throne and the kingdom about 547'; the end year 559 is from the Urien page, 'Ida of Bernicia (547 x 559)'.

rulers.name: Æthelfrith
rulers.note: Killed at the River Idle around 616; also king of Deira from around 604.

correction.text: Ida's kingdom at Bamburgh, drawn as the 555 shape because the page gives no earlier extent

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 547-554 (Cliopatria starts in 555): Ida 'obtained the throne and the kingdom about 547'. The page gives no extent for these years; the 555 shape is used. The page gives the kingdom's extent as 'from the Forth to the Tees', roughly Northumberland, Tyne and Wear, Durham, Berwickshire and East Lothian; by my arithmetic from county areas (not on the page) that is about 10,000 km2, close to the 10,529 km2 of the shape.

555-611, 10,529 km2, bbox lat 54.48-56.05 (Tees to the Forth firth). The infobox has no area. Cliopatria keeps Bernicia and Deira separate until 611 and starts Northumbria in 612; the page dates Æthelfrith's union of Deira 'around 604' (infobox 'shared crown 604'). The ledger carries the 604 vassal_start over Deira (Deira keeps its own shape to 611, so it is not added to this one) and the 612 hand-over to Northumbria; the shape is left as drawn.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 633-634; Bernicia separate again under Eanfrith until Oswald's union in 634

keyframe_review.note: 633 in Cliopatria, one year, 10,529 km2 (the 555 shape again). Years: 'Eanfrith of Bernicia, son of Æthelfrith (633-634)'; Oswald's victory at Heavenfield and the union with Deira are 634. Cliopatria's Northumbria also has a shape from 634, so the successor's shape should take 634 where the two meet. 612-632 are Cliopatria's Northumbria years (Bernicia under the Deiran Edwin, 616-633); the ledger's 612 merge hands the land to Northumbria before this shape returns.

region.text: Bernicia 'from the Forth to the Tees' around Bamburgh

ledger.note: 547: Ida takes the throne of Bernicia, probably at Bamburgh. 'Ida ... obtained the throne and the kingdom about 547' (the page does not say he founded it then); the infobox says only '6th century'. Cliopatria starts the state in 555.

region.text: Deira between the Tees and the Humber, under Æthelfrith's crown but still its own kingdom

ledger.note: c. 604: Æthelfrith takes Deira under his crown. 'Æthelfrith united Deira with his own kingdom by force around 604' and the infobox has 'Shared crown with Deira: 604' (page re-read 2026-10-25); the page adds 'It is unknown when the Angles finally conquered the whole region, but around 604 is likely.' Typed vassal_start, not merge, to agree with the Deira dossier (604 vassal_start with counterpart kingdom-of-bernicia, 612 vassal_end, 612 merge into Northumbria) and with Cliopatria, which keeps Deira's own 12,958 km2 shape to 611 and starts Northumbria in 612; a merge here would draw Deira twice in 604-611. The infobox puts the merger with Deira at 654, the body at 634 under Oswald; the Æthelfrith page (first run) has 'He gained control of Deira around 604; the circumstances of this are unknown'.

region.text: Deira between the Tees and the Humber, under Æthelfrith's crown but still its own kingdom

ledger.note: 612: Deira's separate status under the Bernician crown ends on the map as Cliopatria's Northumbria row begins (one shape of 23,570 km2 from 612 to 616). The page does not date the end of the relation: 'In the early 7th century, it merged with its southern neighbour, Deira, to form the kingdom of Northumbria', infobox 'merged with Deira: 654', 'Bernicia was united with Deira to form Northumbria from 634 onward'. 612 is Cliopatria's year, a bridge; the Deira dossier has the same 612 vassal_end.

region.text: Bernicia from the Forth to the Tees, drawn from 612 inside Cliopatria's Northumbria

ledger.note: 612: Bernicia's land passes into Cliopatria's Northumbria shape, which runs 612-632; the bridge that hands the land over before the 633 gain. The page has the two crowns together from c. 604 ('Shared crown with Deira: 604') and its list marks the years 616-633 as 'Under Deiran rule' (Edwin of Deira); the Æthelfrith page (first run) has Edwin 'became king not just of Deira but of Bernicia as well' after the River Idle, c. 616. The page does not say Bernicia ceased to exist in 612; the dossier's life runs on to 634 and Cliopatria's 633 shape is a one-year Bernicia again under Eanfrith. The Deira dossier carries the matching 612 merge into kingdom-of-northumbria.

633: Bernicia stands alone again under Eanfrith. Edwin 'fell in battle in 633 against Cadwallon of Gwynedd' and Penda (Northumbria page); the Bernicia page lists 'Eanfrith of Bernicia, son of Æthelfrith (633-634)'. Cliopatria shows Bernicia and Deira as separate one-year shapes in 633.

634: Oswald reunites Bernicia and Deira as Northumbria. 'Oswald ... finally defeated Cadwallon at the Battle of Heavenfield in 634'; 'Under Oswald son of Æthelfrith, Bernicia was united with Deira to form Northumbria from 634 onward.'

wars.name: Urien of Rheged's siege of Lindisfarne

zones.text: Lindisfarne (Old Welsh Medcaut) and the Bernician coast

wars.outcome: Urien 'penned the Anglo-Saxons in at Lindisfarne' and Theodric was 'besieged ... on Lindisfarne'; Urien was then killed at the instigation of Morgan (Morcant). No land changed hands.
wars.note: The years are the Historia Brittonum synchronisms with Theodric (572-579) and Hussa (585-592) as given on the Urien page; the page says Urien's death 'could have happened as early as 572 AD to as late as after Augustine's mission' in 597.

wars.name: Battle of Catraeth
wars.outcome: 'In around 600 the Gododdin raised a force of about 300 men to assault the Angle stronghold of Catraeth, perhaps Catterick, North Yorkshire. The battle, which ended disastrously for the Britons, was memorialised in the poem Y Gododdin.' No land changed hands on the page.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered. The Gododdin page calls Catraeth an 'Angle stronghold' and never names the Anglian kingdom (not Bernicia, not Deira); Bernicia is named only for the later conquest ('the Gododdin seem to have come under the rule of Bernicia around this time', of the 638 siege of Eidyn). Catterick is not on a Bernicia page, so Bernician involvement is not shown; the Deira and Northumbria dossiers may claim it. Siege of Din Eidyn 638: 'In 638, Eidyn, modern Edinburgh, was under siege and fell to the Angles' (same page); it lies after this dossier's 634 end and is Northumbria's, so it is not a war here.

wars.name: Battle of Degsastan
wars.outcome: Bede reports Æthelfrith won 'a crushing victory at a place called Degsastan' over Áedán mac Gabráin of Dál Riata, who led 'an immense and mighty army'.

wars.name: Battle of Chester
wars.outcome: Æthelfrith 'defeated its army in a battle at Chester', probably between 613 and 616; no land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Battle of the River Idle
wars.outcome: 'around 616 Æthelfrith was defeated and killed at the Battle of the River Idle'; Edwin 'became king not just of Deira but of Bernicia as well'.
wars.note: The Northumbria page says Edwin returned about 616 'to conquer Northumbria with Rædwald's aid'.

wars.name: Battle of Heavenfield
wars.outcome: Oswald 'finally defeated Cadwallon at the Battle of Heavenfield in 634' and united Bernicia with Deira.

certainty.note: The Forth, Tees and Pennine frontiers are approximate; no source fixes a line.

notes:
Kingdom of Bernicia (2 Cliopatria shapes, 555-611 and 633), budget 1-2 pages; five pages opened because the Urien, Northumbria and Chester pages were read for neighbouring dossiers.
LIFE vs CLIOPATRIA: the dossier runs 547-634 (Ida to Oswald). Cliopatria draws Bernicia 555-611 and 633 only; 612-632 are its Northumbria years, though the pages have Bernicia a separate crown (Edwin of Deira king of both, 616-633). I did not add a keyframe for 612-632 so that Bernicia is not drawn twice; the Northumbria dossier owns those years. The Deira link is a 604 vassal_start (Deira keeps its own shape) closed by a 612 vassal_end, then a 612 merge of Bernicia's land into Northumbria, both mirroring the Deira dossier; 604 is a page date, 612 is Cliopatria's map convention (repair pass after review: the first draft had a 604 merge that drew Deira twice).
END YEAR: 634 on the page; Cliopatria's Northumbria also has a shape from 634. The rendering should let the successor's shape win in 634.
Repair pass opened Gododdin: Catraeth 'in around 600' is a war entry (the page names no Anglian kingdom there); the 638 siege of Eidyn is after the 634 end and is left to Northumbria, though the page says the Gododdin 'seem to have come under the rule of Bernicia around this time', which fits the infobox's 654 merger better than the 634 end. Not opened: Bamburgh.
Infobox discrepancy: the Bernicia infobox gives 654 for the merger with Deira, the body gives 634 under Oswald; the Northumbria page gives 654 for the union of crowns and 651 for 'united under Bernician rule' after Oswine's murder.
